- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–2% to match recent momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; force a mean-reversion correction: average last 5–7 days’ true values and use as anchor for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate near-term (1–7 days) and underestimate long-term (15–30 days) — apply a “tail correction”: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per 10-day horizon beyond 10 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3–5-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
